title.narrative: Climate Action Window (CAW) in the African Development Fund (ADF)

description.narrative: Core funding to Climate Action Window (CAW) in the African Development Fund (ADF), the soft window of the African Development Bank (AfDB). CAW provides grant finance to all countries that are eligible for support from the African Development Fund, to enhance access to climate finance beyond the existing efforts of the Bank in allocating 40% of its resources to Climate Action. The CAW is structured around three sub-windows: adaptation, mitigation, and technical assistance (TA). The aspirational allocation of funding between these sub-windows is 75% for adaptation, 15% for mitigation, and 10% for TA. Norway supports the adaptation subwindow. CAW Projects are drawn from existing ADF pipelines, national climate plans, Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), or co-developed with partners and other Bank Group initiatives through competitive calls. Projects must demonstrate host country ownership and significant co-financing potential as the goal of the CAW is to leverage up to three times its resource pool. All projects financed by the CAW must align with the Paris Agreement (“Paris-aligned”) for carbon neutral pathways and climate resilient development outcomes. Projects should originate from one or more of six CAW priority sectors, namely: (i) agriculture, food security and nutrition; (ii) water security and sanitation; (iii) climate information, early warning, and disaster risk management; (iv) transport and infrastructure; (v) energy access and renewable energy; and (vi) green finance.
